 CORAM : V. M. DESHPANDE, J.
 DATE : July 29, 2019 ORAL JUDGMENT :
1] Heard Shri J. B. Kasat, the learned counsel for the appellant- The Corporation of the City of Nagpur.

By the present appeal, the appellant is challenging the judgment and order of acquittal passed by NAMRATA Judg.Cril.apeal55-2005.odt the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Nagpur in Regular Criminal Case No. 13/1993.

By the impugned judgment, both the accused against The Corporation Of The City Of Nagpur vs Vilas Dadaraoji Deshmukh And ... on 29 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126401985/
1 whom charge was framed were acquitted for the offence punishable under Section 7(i) read with Section 2(ia) (a), Section 7 (ii) read with Section 2 (ix)(d), Section 7(v) read with Rule 23, Section 7(v) read with Rule 50, punishable under Section 16 (1) (a)
(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules,
1955.
2] During the pendency of this appeal, respondent No.1-Vilas Deshmukh expired and therefore, vide order dated 14/02/2019 appeal against him was ordered to be abated.
3] At the time of hearing of this appeal, counsel for the respondent No.2 choose not to remain present before the Court.

sentences.text: 4] In order to prove charge, prosecution examined two witnesses.
They are PW-1-Shrikrushna S/o. Jadhavji Rajankar and PW-2 Dr. Suryakant S/o. Govindrao Kimmatkar.

Star witness is PW-1- Shrikrushna Rajankar, who was at the relevant time a Food Inspector and who h a s e x e r c i s e d p o w e r s i n t h e s a i d c a p a c i t y a n d f o r t h e c o m p l a i n t N A M R A T A Judg.Cril.apeal55-2005.odt PW-2-Dr. Suryakant Kimmatkar's evidence is not material for deciding the present case.
5] Shrikrushna Rajankar (PW-1) stood retired from the services in the year 1999.
From 1985 till his retirement he was working as Food Inspector in Nagpur Municipal Corporation.

6] On 01/12/1992,
he paid a visit to New M.L.A. Canteen, Nagpur along with Panch-Rajesh Sabale, who was not examined during the trial.
At that time, deceased respondent-Vilas Deshmukh was present.
Shri Shrikrushna Rajankar gave his identification and inspected the canteen.
He prepared inspection report and gave a copy to Shri Vilas Deshmukh.
The copy of the report is at Exh. 30.
7] During inspection, he found one open chilly powder bag containing about 5 Kg. without label.
On inquiry deceased Vilas Deshmukh disclosed that the said chilly powder is used for preparing eatables and other food articles.
Complainant disclosed his intention to deceased accused and obtained sample of said chilly powder.
Six Hundred grams of chilly powder was taken.
It was put in a pot.
Rupees twenty seven was paid towards price of the said chilly powder.
The NAMRATA Judg.Cril.apeal55-2005.odt receipt was executed, it is at Exh. 31.
8] Thereafter, complainant prepared three copies of Form No.VI.
One was given to the accused/deceased.
Office copy of Form No.VI is at Exh. 32.
Thereafter, the complainant prepared three copies of the notice under Section 14-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Original was given to deceased Vilas Deshmukh and the office copy having his signature is at Exh.33.
9] Complainant divided 600 grams of chilly powder in three equal parts and taken in three glass bottles and put lead on each glass bottle.
Thereafter, seal was prepared.

Thereafter, he returned to the office and under the sealed condition the articles were sent to the Public Analyst,
Regional Public Health Laboratory, Nagpur.
On 06/01/1993 complainant received report from Public Analyst, Regional Public Health Laboratory, Nagpur.
Report is at Exh. 43.
It does not show that the chilly powder was confirming standard.
Thereafter, following other usual steps the complaint was filed.

It would be relevant to reproduce herein paragraph 21 from the evidence of complainant and it is reproduced herein:

sentences.text: 2 NAMRATA Judg.Cril.apeal55-2005.odt "21.
I did not record the statement of accused no.2.
I took sample bottles from Store of Health Dept. prior to four or five days on 1/12/1992.
The sample bottles were not sterilized.
I have not washed, clean and dryed the sample bottles in spot.
22. I have not covered the mouth of sample bottles, sealing by the Wax.
The lead put on the sample bottles was of plastic.
That plastic cork was not of I.S.I. Marked or Grade.
I do not know, whether plastic material without I.S.I. Mark, if comes in to contact with the food articles, then food articles does not remain fit for human consumption.
It is not true to say that, thread on the paper needs to be fasten by means of sealing wax.
I have not fasten the entire thread by sealing wax, on the paper cover."
10] It is also an admitted position on record that panchanama (Exh.35) was not supplied to the accused persons.

11] In view of the admission as given by the complainant, the learned counsel for the appellant fairly states that the mandatory provisions of Rule 16 and 14 were not properly followed by the complainant.

The learned Chief Judicial Magistrate in my view has not NAMRATA Judg.Cril.apeal55-2005.odt committed any mistake while acquitting the accused persons, especially when the mandatory provisions of sealing and taking the sample in a dry clean jar were not followed.

sentences.text: 12] By now, the law on the aspect of appeal against acquittal is well settled.

Merely because another view is possible that is not sufficient for Appellate Court to substitute its own view in place of view taken by the Court below, if the view taken by the Trial Court is based on available evidence and appreciation of the evidence in accordance with law.
In the present case, no perversity can locate in the order of the acquittal.
Consequently, there is no merit in the appeal.
Appeal fails and the same is dismissed.
